title: What does the job cost?
instruction: Examine the office offer. Challenge its assumptions, then negotiate a workable arrangement

video.title: The First Guy To Ever Work In An Office

items.prompt: What imbalance does the pay offer create?
items.hint: Compare what he must help the employer earn with what he receives
items.answer: He must help the employer make a lot of money, but the employer promises to give him only a small part of it

items.prompt: Why do mornings, evenings and two days off fail to settle his concern?
items.hint: Distinguish free hours from energy to use them
items.answer: He expects to be tired before and after work, and the weekend is described as enough for one activity followed by recovery for the next week

items.prompt: What is ironic about the office with a view and the golden years?
items.hint: Compare the positive labels with how much control he has over his time
items.answer: Both are presented as rewards, but they leave the main cost in place: a window lets him see a day he cannot enjoy, and full control of his time is postponed until much later in life

items.prompt: How would you challenge one assumption and negotiate a workable schedule?
items.hint: Name the assumption, acknowledge a work need and propose a specific boundary
items.answer: Example: I can commit to agreed deadlines, but time at a desk does not prove useful output. Could we agree on core hours and keep evenings free except for genuine emergencies?
